title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is an undisclosed synthetic alteration of a photograph of real people, deployed in public-facing advertising. A student who had been in the original image was removed and replaced with a different person, and other students in the frame were digitally reshaped. The output was presented as a photograph of a Stanford event rather than as an edited image, so the alteration was invisible to anyone who saw the banners.

The failure sits at the point where an edited asset moves from production into published material. Stanford's own policy already prohibited using AI to create or alter images of Stanford people, events, facilities or achievements, so the rule that would have stopped it existed before the banner was made. What was missing was a check at publication: someone comparing the final asset against the source photo, or confirming that the edit had been disclosed, would have caught it without any new policy. The university has said it is adding training and review of materials.

It is not established who performed the edit, whether the alteration was intended to misrepresent the student's race, or what consequences, if any, followed. The university confirmed the AI use and called it a policy violation, which is a finding about the act and not about anyone's intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, a Stanford University photographer took a picture of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, with two other students at a Lunar New Year party. The dining service posted it online. When Stanford used the image on banners in 2026, Ramirez had been replaced by a Black woman, and the other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez learned about the change from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated, though he also saw a comedic side.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to change the original photo. The university said its policy bans using A.I. to create or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and to make sure all materials are properly reviewed.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
